note: Mirror merge rules of sync-v1 (docs/sync-v1.md "Merge rules"). Songs are named by the keys of "songs"; HLCs are [wallMs, counter, deviceId]. Frozen: see "Test vectors".

apply.name: a remote like is added
a newer op wins
an older op loses
same wall: the counter decides
same wall and counter: the larger device id wins
same wall and counter, smaller device id: loses
device ids compare by code unit (upper case before lower)
an echo of the same op changes nothing
matched by sameSong: the record keeps its own song
two ISRCs are two songs
a tombstone for an unknown song is kept, so an older like can't bring it back
ops apply in order, each against the result so far
records keep their order; new ones follow in op order

diff.name: matched across the ISRC and words keys
a Spotify/YTM like after a mirrored unlike is not sent back
a new Spotify/YTM like is sent
a tombstone and no like: nothing
likes in liked order, then unlikes in base order

apply.name: a remote play is added with its origin, newest first
one play under the ISRC key and the words key: once
the same song at another start: a second play
older than the clear mark: dropped (the mark itself is kept)
clearPlays removes older plays and raises the mark
a lower clear mark changes nothing
in order: a clear after a play removes it
a tie on playedAt keeps existing plays first

diff.name: own plays not in the base
plays from another device never go back
plays under the clear mark are not sent

merge.name: a new playlist from the space
fast-forward: the remote edit started from this version
local unchanged since the base: take the remote
unchanged is judged by sameSong (ISRC and words keys)
the remote is the base again (an echo): keep local
add / add: the newer side orders, the other side's song follows its neighbour
add / remove (the manual script's step 7)
remove / remove
reorder (newer) / add
reorder (older) / add: the newer edit's order wins
an addition with no surviving neighbour before it goes to the start
an addition after a song the other side removed follows the next surviving neighbour back
the same song added on both sides is kept once
several additions keep their order
repeats pair by occurrence: removing the second copy
repeats pair by occurrence: first with first, so removing the first copy reads as removing the last
name: the side that renamed it wins, even when older
name: both renamed, the newer wins
a delete beats an older concurrent edit
an edit newer than the delete survives (and is pushed back)
a delete, local unchanged
deleted here, edited there later: it comes back with the edit
deleted here after the edit there: stays deleted
deleted here, the remote is the base again: stays deleted
deleted on both sides
a followed mix: the higher version wins, songs are not merged
a followed mix, same version: the newer edit wins
a followed mix unfollowed and edited here, newer: kept as a plain playlist
read-only on the web: the phone's op is taken, whatever the clocks
read-only on the web: another browser's op is ignored
read-only on the phone: ops from a browser are ignored
a new read-only playlist from the phone appears on the web
no common base: both sides' songs are kept
